name: Tarragon

schedule.notes: ALWAYS get French Tarragon from a cutting or division — true French sets no viable seed. Russian Tarragon is seed-grown but flavorless.
Snip leafy tops. Avoid heavy harvest in year 1. Flavor peaks just before flowering.

harvest.cues: Leaves bright green, narrow, soft. Snip whole stems just above a leaf node.
harvest.storageNotes: Best fresh or preserved in vinegar (classic tarragon vinegar). Drying loses most of the flavor.

varieties.name: French Tarragon
varieties.notes: Real anise-licorice flavor. The only culinary tarragon. Propagate by cuttings or division only.

notes: Reject anything sold as 'tarragon seed' — it's Russian Tarragon, flavorless. Divide French Tarragon every 3 to 4 years to keep it vigorous. Mulch in zone 4 to overwinter.
